title: RV & Boat Storage Fundamentals
description: Why vehicle owners need us, how to tell RV classes and boat types apart, open, covered and enclosed spaces and the shape of a space, each Greens site's lot, measuring so a vehicle fits the first time, the paperwork every vehicle needs (including non-running and PNO vehicles), lot rules and the lot walk, the vehicle lien path, and how to sell and keep vehicle tenants.
overview: Why vehicle storage matters at Greens and who the customers are
RV classes and boat types, with real lengths and heights
Open, covered and enclosed spaces, drive-in and pull-through, and each Greens site's lot
Measuring and checking clearance so a vehicle fits the first time
The paperwork every vehicle needs, including non-running and PNO vehicles
Lot rules, blocks and chocks, and the lot walk
The vehicle and boat lien path from the 61st day
Selling, waitlists, upgrades and keeping vehicle tenants

questions.q: A caller says, "It's a 28-foot travel trailer." What do you ask next?
options: Is that the box, or hitch to bumper?
Great, so a 10x30 will work for you?
What year, make and color is it?
Would you like covered or open space?
questions.explanation: A travel trailer's stated length may leave out the 3 to 5 ft tongue and anything on the back. Quoting a 10x30 on the brochure number is the classic wrong fit.

questions.q: A walk-in describes a motorhome with a truck cab and a sleeping bunk built out over the cab. What is it?
questions.explanation: A cab with a bunk over it is a Class C. A Class A has a flat bus front; a Class B looks like a van; a fifth wheel has no engine at all.

questions.q: A customer wants covered space for a fifth wheel. Which height do you need from them?
options: To the top of the air conditioner
To the roof line given in the brochure
To the top of the side windows
The height printed on the registration
questions.explanation: Under a roof, what hits the beam is the tallest thing on the roof: the air conditioner, antenna or dome. The brochure roof line is too low by 10 inches or more.

questions.q: A caller wants a 20 ft space for a "20 ft bass boat." On the trailer, tongue tip to the motor, it is 26 ft. What fits?
options: A space of 29 ft or more
questions.explanation: Plan for the length on the trailer plus a 3 ft margin: 26 + 3 = 29 ft. The hull length (LOA) leaves out the tongue and the motor.

questions.q: A boat's advertised length (LOA) includes its outboard motor and its trailer tongue.
questions.explanation: LOA is the hull only, bow to stern. The tongue, the motor's lower unit and a swim platform add several feet, so you measure tongue tip to the rearmost point.

questions.q: A wake boat owner wants a covered space. Which can change the boat's height on its trailer? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Towers, biminis and T-tops all raise the height under a roof. A swim platform adds length at the stern, not height.

questions.q: A Class A arrives towing a small car behind it. How do you treat the car?
questions.explanation: A towed car (a toad) is a separate vehicle: it needs its own space and its own line on the lease, or it leaves with the owner. It never sits in the aisle.

questions.q: A caller says, "My HOA gave me ten days to move my trailer." What do you lead with?
questions.explanation: You never comment on HOA rules. Speed matters to this caller, so you start the fit check (length first) and find a space that fits before the deadline.

questions.q: A customer stores two jet skis on one trailer. What goes on the lease?
options: The trailer and both jet skis
Only the two jet skis themselves
questions.explanation: A jet ski trailer is a trailer with its own registration, and each jet ski is registered craft. All three go on the lease with their numbers.

questions.q: A tenant who asks to sleep one night in his stored RV before an early trip is told no.
questions.explanation: Greens never allows living or sleeping in a stored vehicle, even for one night. A vehicle left after closing is locked in until the next business day.

questions.q: A travel trailer's box is 28 ft. The tongue adds 4 ft and a bike rack adds 1 ft. What is its storage length before any margin?
questions.explanation: Storage length is hitch to bumper with everything on the back: 28 + 4 + 1 = 33 ft. Then add the 3 to 4 ft margin to pick the space.

questions.q: At Fairfield a trailer measures 34 ft hitch to bumper. With a 3 ft margin, which size do you quote?
questions.explanation: 34 + 3 = 37 ft. Fairfield's sizes jump from 32 ft to 48 ft, so the 12x32 is too short even before the margin and the 12x48 is the next size up.

questions.q: A 36 ft Class A (with its ladder) wants a drive-in at Escondido. Which is the smallest space that fits with a 3 ft margin?
questions.explanation: 36 + 3 = 39 ft, so the 12x38 is 1 ft short and the 12x40 is the smallest that fits. A 12x50 fits too but uses a long space a longer rig needs.

questions.q: At Temecula a wake boat is 31 ft on its trailer. Covered sizes are 10x20, 11x30, 12x35, 12x40 and 12x50. Which is the smallest covered space that fits?
questions.explanation: 31 + 3 = 34 ft, so the 11x30 is too short and the 12x35 is the smallest covered space that fits. Height is checked separately against the covered rows' clear height.

questions.q: A fifth wheel is 13 ft 6 in to the top of its air conditioners. No clear height is posted at the covered rows. What do you do?
options: Let the tenant try it slowly
questions.explanation: Never guess and never let a tenant try it: the test is the damage. Your manager has the clear heights until the site profile is filled in; until you know, offer open space.

questions.q: An enclosed garage door is sold as 14 ft high. What do you plan for?
options: Height does not matter in a garage
questions.explanation: A door sold as 14 ft may measure about 13 ft 8 in once hung, and a rain lip can take another inch. Measure the actual opening.

questions.q: A tenant backs a boat trailer into a drive-in space. Which way should it face?
questions.explanation: Tongue to the aisle means the tow vehicle backs to the coupler in the aisle and pulls straight out next time. Nosed in, every hook-up is a blind reverse out of a dead end.

questions.q: A Class A is backed in until its rear tires touch the wheel stop, with a fence 3 ft behind the stop. What is the risk?
options: The front sits out in the drive aisle
questions.explanation: A wheel stop marks the tires, not the body. A Class A's rear overhang can be 8 to 12 ft, which reaches a fence 3 ft away.

questions.q: A customer at Murrieta hates backing and has a 42 ft fifth wheel. What do you check for first?
questions.explanation: Murrieta's 12x50s are all pull-through: a 42 ft rig plus margin fits, and nobody backs more than a truck length. Murrieta has no covered spaces, and the others are too short.

questions.q: Put the start of the fit-check conversation in order.
options: What is the overall length, hitch to bumper?
For covered: what is the height to the top?
Does it have slides, or does the tongue fold?
How do you usually park it?
questions.explanation: Type first, then the length that decides the space, then height for a roof, then width and folding parts, then how they park, which tells you whether to offer a pull-through.

questions.q: A walk-in at Fairfield asks why he should pay for gravel when the street is free. What do you do first?
options: Quote the city code on street parking
Ask what happens with it today
Offer the lowest rate right away
questions.explanation: Find the reason they cannot park at home: here a neighbor complaint and a stolen battery. That tells you to lead with the gate and the walks. Never quote city code.

questions.q: A caller at Valley Center wants to store a 30 ft boat. What do you do?
options: Put the boat on Valley Center's waitlist only
Check Escondido and Temecula in Cubby
Offer a large storage unit for it
Tell them Greens has no boat storage
questions.explanation: Valley Center has almost no vehicle space. Knowing which sister site can fit a caller, and checking it in Cubby first, keeps the customer with Greens.

questions.q: A caller says, "I have a 36-foot fifth wheel." Which number might be missing from that length?
questions.explanation: A fifth wheel's 3 to 5 ft pin box overhang may not be in the stated length. Measure from the front of the nose or pin box to the rear bumper.

questions.q: At Murrieta, a fifth wheel measures 39 ft with its pin box. Which spaces do you look at?
options: Two 10x24s side by side in a row
questions.explanation: 39 + 3 = 42 ft. Murrieta's 10 ft wide spaces stop at 35 ft; the 12x45 drive-ins and the 12x50 pull-throughs are long enough.

questions.q: A caller asks for a space for a truck camper they want to leave on its jacks off the truck. What is Greens' rule?
options: Allowed if the jacks have pads
questions.explanation: Greens Vehicle Storage Rules: a truck camper stored off the truck on its jacks needs the manager's OK. Ask the length with and without the truck.

questions.q: A 22 ft sailboat is 30 ft on its trailer, and the mast sticks 3 ft past the stern. With a 3 ft margin, what length do you need?
questions.explanation: The mast overhang counts: 30 + 3 = 33 ft in the space, plus a 3 ft margin = 36 ft. At Escondido a 12x38 fits.

questions.q: A customer brings a boat on its trailer. Which registrations do you need?
options: The boat's, then the trailer's later
Only the boat's, if it is new
questions.explanation: A boat and its trailer are registered separately, and both go on the lease. One registration is not enough for either to go in.

questions.q: A swing (folding) trailer tongue can shorten a boat's storage length by a few feet.
questions.explanation: Some makers list a towing length and a storage length. Folding the tongue can save a few feet, which can be the difference between two space sizes.

questions.q: Under a canopy, where is the clear height measured?
options: To the top of the end posts
questions.explanation: Clear height is to the lowest point a rig must pass under: the beam, not the roof sheet. That beam is what tears off an air conditioner.

questions.q: A customer at Escondido wants covered space for a fifth wheel. What do you tell them?
options: Escondido has a few covered rows
Covered is at every Greens site
questions.explanation: Temecula has the only covered spaces at Greens. Offer open space at Escondido now, or check Temecula's covered spaces and waitlist.

questions.q: A covered space keeps blowing rain and dust off a vehicle.
questions.explanation: A canopy is a roof with open sides. It blocks sun, UV and hail, but blowing rain, dust and low afternoon sun still reach the vehicle. Sell it honestly.

questions.q: Why are pull-through spaces scarce and priced above drive-ins?
options: Every one of them comes with a canopy
questions.explanation: A pull-through needs an aisle at each end, so a lot gives up spaces to make one. That convenience (no backing) is why it costs more.

questions.q: A tenant enters an angled row against its arrows. What happens?
options: Nothing; either direction works the same
questions.explanation: An angled space is a gentle curve only from the right direction. Against the arrows every space is a jackknife turn; faded arrows are worth a same-day report.

questions.q: A long rig with a nervous driver has no pull-through open. What do you offer?
options: The corner space where rows meet
An end space on a wide aisle
A space two sizes too short
questions.explanation: An end space has one neighbor and an easier turn. A corner space is the hardest turn on the lot. Add the pull-through waitlist too.

questions.q: Which best describes Fairfield's parking?
options: Paved, with covered rows at the back
questions.explanation: Fairfield is all open gravel, every space 12 ft wide, 20 to 48 ft deep, with no covered or enclosed vehicle space.

questions.q: A tenant at Fairfield says his gate code failed last night. Where can you check what happened?
options: The Nexus Report a Problem log
questions.explanation: Fairfield's gate reports to Cubby: allowed entries, refused codes and after-hours attempts. That makes it the one gate log you can check yourself.

questions.q: A Murrieta tenant has a 37 ft trailer and wants a 12 ft wide drive-in. Which size fits with a margin?
questions.explanation: 37 + 3 = 40 ft. Murrieta's 12x45s are drive-ins long enough; the 12x30 and 12x33 are too short, and the 10x35 is too short and narrow.

questions.q: A Murrieta customer is billed monthly under a "Dump Station Agreement" with no size. What is it?
options: A late fee by another name
questions.explanation: Murrieta's Dump Station Agreement entries in Cubby are not storage: they bill a customer for monthly use of the site's dump station.

questions.q: Every other Greens lot is full for a 40 ft rig. Which site most often has a long open space?
questions.explanation: Temecula has the most open spaces 40 ft and longer at Greens, most of them 11x40, and is the usual backup for big rigs.

questions.q: A caller at Escondido asks to park a car in one of the big 15 ft wide storage units. What do you say?
options: Yes, the big units fit cars well
questions.explanation: The large units are not set up for vehicles in Cubby, so you never offer one for a vehicle. Offer an open space; your manager has whether that will change.

questions.q: A collector wants an enclosed garage for a classic car. Where at Greens is enclosed vehicle space?
questions.explanation: Valley Center's two 12x38 garages are Greens' only enclosed vehicle spaces, and they are usually leased: take a full waitlist entry and offer open space meanwhile.

questions.q: A rig that fits a garage door advertised as 14 ft tall is sure to clear the opening.
questions.explanation: A door is smaller once hung, and a rain lip takes more. The rig must fit the measured opening; your manager has it until the site profile is filled in.

questions.q: A "26 ft Class C" at Murrieta is 28 ft with its ladder and rack. Is a 10x30 right?
options: Yes, it is 2 ft longer than the rig
No, it needs 31 ft or more
Yes, if it parks nose in
questions.explanation: 28 + 3 = 31 ft, so the 10x30 is too tight. A 12x33 or 10x35, if open, fits without wasting a 50 ft space.

questions.q: A 36 ft boat is 41 ft on its trailer. Can it go in a Valley Center 12x38 garage?
options: Yes, if the door is tall enough
Yes, with the tongue in the aisle
questions.explanation: 41 ft on the trailer is longer than the 38 ft garage before any margin. Length rules out the space whatever the door height.

questions.q: Which clear height decides whether a rig can reach a covered space?
options: The beam over the space itself
The lowest point on the path
questions.explanation: Check the whole route: the gate, any overhead structure and the beam over the space. The lowest point on the path is the one that counts.

questions.q: When the tape on move-in day differs from the phone call, you keep the caller's numbers in Cubby.
questions.explanation: The tape on move-in day is the record. Update Cubby with the measured length and height so the next person never has to ask again.

questions.q: The VIN on a customer's insurance card does not match the registration. What do you do?
questions.explanation: A mismatch is a stop: nothing goes in until the numbers match on every document. Often the customer swapped vehicles and never updated the policy.

questions.q: A tenant asks who pays if his RV is damaged on the lot. What is true?
questions.explanation: The tenant's own vehicle insurance covers the vehicle. Greens' property insurance does not, and the protection plan does not cover vehicles. Never say "you're covered here."

questions.q: A tenant's car is on Planned Non-Operation. He plans to tow it out on Saturday. What do you tell him?
options: Only Greens can tow it out
Leave the sticker as it is
questions.explanation: PNO means the vehicle is not driven, towed, stored or parked on a public road. Before it leaves on one, even on a tow truck, the owner registers it again with the DMV.

questions.q: A customer wants to store a car on Planned Non-Operation. What do you ask for?
options: Nothing beyond the usual photo ID
DMV proof PNO is on file
questions.explanation: Ask for proof from the DMV that PNO is on file in the tenant's name, plus ID and insurance; note PNO and the year in Cubby. It needs your manager's OK.

questions.q: Which photos belong in a vehicle move-in set? Choose all that apply.
options: All four sides of the vehicle
The plate and the VIN or HIN
questions.explanation: Photos are the baseline for any later talk about damage, leaks or abandonment. You do not search or photograph inside a tenant's vehicle.

questions.q: Someone not on the lease arrives to drive a tenant's RV out. What do you do?
options: Let them go if they know the gate code
Stop and check with your manager
questions.explanation: Only authorized drivers listed on the lease take a vehicle out. Stop, check with your manager, and never confirm to the visitor that anyone is a tenant.

questions.q: A tenant asks if he may keep a full gas can in his trailer for the generator. What is Greens' rule?
options: Yes, one can per space is allowed
questions.explanation: No gasoline, diesel or propane containers unless empty and disconnected, and tanks under 1/4 full. A generator also needs written permission.

questions.q: A tenant takes his RV out for a week and parks his car in the space meanwhile. What is the rule?
options: Fine, as long as the RV is away
Fine if the car is smaller
Fine for under a month at a time
questions.explanation: Only the vehicle on the lease holds the space, and the tenant tells the office if it will be away more than 24 hours.

questions.q: A tenant may change a flat tire on his trailer in his space.
questions.explanation: Work that makes a vehicle road-ready, such as a tire or battery change, is allowed. Repairs, fluid changes and major mechanical work are not.

questions.q: On a walk you smell gas near a motorhome. What do you do first?
questions.explanation: Gas or smoke: leave the area and call 911 first, then tell your manager. Never shut off a tenant's propane or move their vehicle yourself.

questions.q: A tenant is changing his oil in his space. Which sentence works best?
options: "Rules are rules, so stop right now."
questions.explanation: Lead with the reason, not the rule: oil and coolant end up in the storm drain. Then suggest a shop, note it in Cubby and tell your manager.

questions.q: After rain at Fairfield, a trailer has rolled off one chock and rests on a neighbor's bumper. What do you do?
options: Push it back into its own space gently
Leave a note on the trailer
questions.explanation: You never chock, block or move a tenant's vehicle. Keep people clear, photograph both, call both tenants and tell your manager.

questions.q: Which may a tenant leave in the space with a parked trailer?
options: A spare set of tires for the trailer
The blocks and chocks under it
questions.explanation: Trailers sit on wood blocks with the wheels chocked and a hitch lock on. Spare tires, ramps and loose lumber are items beside the vehicle, which are not allowed.

questions.q: A car has expired tags by eight months and its Cubby note says PNO. What does that tell you?
options: It is abandoned, so start a vehicle lien
The sticker alone is not a sign
It must leave the lot today
questions.explanation: A PNO vehicle's sticker looks expired by design. Expired tags are an abandonment sign only with other signs, such as flats, no visits and a late account.

questions.q: You find a car with no lease parked in an empty space. What do you do?
options: Photograph, check Cubby, tell your manager
Boot it until someone calls the office about it
questions.explanation: A vehicle with no lease is not a lien case, and you never tow, boot or tag on your own. Photograph it, check Cubby, and tell your manager.

questions.q: On your walk the gate closes before long rigs clear it. Where does that go?
options: A note on a tenant's lease
questions.explanation: Site problems go through Nexus: scan the site's QR tag and use Report a Problem (or file a ticket), where maintenance sees it with the photo, place and time.

questions.q: Your manager wants each lot walk recorded. Where do you fill it in?
options: A paper sheet in the office
questions.explanation: The walk goes on the form your manager picks in Workday's Fill a Form (Inspection or Vehicle Check). It works with no signal and keeps the photos with the place and time.

questions.q: Put the damage incident steps in order.
options: Make sure everyone is safe; 911 if needed
File the Incident Report the same day
questions.explanation: Safety first, then evidence while it is fresh, then the people and their insurers, then the report the same day, then your manager, who decides about Greens' insurer.

questions.q: A tenant clips a bollard and asks, "You'll cover this, right?" What do you say?
options: "Yes, it's our post, so we'll pay."
questions.explanation: Never admit fault or promise payment, either way. Document everything and pass it on; your manager and the insurers decide.

questions.q: A finding on a lot walk with no photo is hard to prove in a later dispute.
questions.explanation: Every exception gets a dated photo and a note. A problem with no photo did not happen, as far as a later dispute is concerned.

questions.q: A coworker suggests adding a defaulted car to next week's unit auction. What is right?
options: Fine, as long as the car still runs
Vehicles never go to that auction
questions.explanation: A titled vehicle or boat never goes through the unit auction: a buyer could not register it, and the lender was never told. Tell your manager.

questions.q: Cubby raises "61st - Vehicle Lien Filing/Tow Notice" on a trailer. What do you do?
options: Call a tow company to come out today
questions.explanation: The task goes to your manager. You gather the lease, VIN, plate, lienholders and insurance, and photograph the trailer's condition now.

questions.q: Under California law, when may a defaulted trailer be towed instead of sold?
options: Whenever the manager decides it should go
questions.explanation: Rent 60 days unpaid, the preliminary lien notice sent, and at least 10 days' notice by first-class mail with a certificate of mailing naming the tow company.

questions.q: A tenant 50 days behind says, "Just keep the boat, I'm done." What do you do?
options: Treat it as a signed release from the tenant
Write it down, tell your manager
Move the boat to the back
questions.explanation: "Keep it" is never permission. Write down exactly what was said and when, and pass it to your manager.

questions.q: In Texas, a defaulted vehicle may be towed to a licensed vehicle storage facility only if the written lease authorizes towing.
questions.explanation: Texas also requires no payment by the 14th day after notice and the facility's written agreement; the lien then ends. Greens' Texas sites are run by CubeSmart.

questions.q: A caller asks the monthly price of a 12x32 at Fairfield. Where does the rate you quote come from?
questions.explanation: Quote today's rate from Cubby, never from a page or memory. Specials and increases change rates.

questions.q: A caller says the place down the road is $40 cheaper. What do you do?
options: End the call politely and move on
questions.explanation: Ask about aisles, hours, surface and amenities, then show what Greens offers. Never criticize a competitor.

questions.q: A caller asks if Greens covers damage to his RV; you may tell him the site's insurance covers vehicles on the lot.
questions.explanation: The tenant's own vehicle insurance covers the vehicle, and Greens needs proof of it at move-in. Never say "we're insured" or "you're covered here."

questions.q: A caller says, "My battery was stolen in my driveway." What do you lead with?
questions.explanation: Listen for the trigger. A theft means security is the sale: the gate code, lighting and the walks. Never promise nothing will happen.

questions.q: A customer wants covered space at Temecula and none is open. What keeps the customer?
options: Ask them to call back later
Open space now, then the waitlist
Park under a canopy in the drive aisle
questions.explanation: Open now, covered later: rent an open space that fits today, add them to the covered waitlist with length and height, and upgrade with a transfer when one opens.

questions.q: Which belong in a vehicle waitlist entry so you can make an offer that fits? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: A waitlist entry needs the fit details (type, length, height, product, sites) so you can call and say "I have your space" without a second fit check.

questions.q: A snowbird will be gone November to March and wants to cancel. What do you say?
options: The space is held for her free of charge
It may not be there in March
questions.explanation: The rental is month to month, so she may leave, but the space may be leased when she returns. Offer the waitlist for her return date and let her decide.

questions.q: On move-in day the tape shows the trailer is 2 ft longer than the caller said. What does the job aid say to do?
options: Ignore it, as long as it still fits
questions.explanation: The last fit-check step is to write the real measurements in Cubby and tape on move-in day. If it still fits with the margin, nothing else changes.

questions.q: A customer says his motorhome will have a "toad" with it. What is that?
questions.explanation: A toad (or dinghy) is a car towed behind a motorhome. It is a separate vehicle and usually needs its own space.
